3. In the auction held before filing of the Writ Petition No. 995 of 2004 in respect of the property mortgaged by the borrower and the Petitioner, the quoted price was found at Taka 48,16,000. After disposal of the said Writ Petitions, the Respondent Bank proposed the highest bidder to purchase 8 decimals of land mortgaged by the borrower Anil Kumar at the price of Taka 24,08,000, but the highest bidder did not come forward to purchase the said property as it was not partitioned. Thereafter, the Bank offered the property to Respondent No.5 at the price quoted by the highest bidder. The Respondent No.5 by a letter though expressed his willingness to purchase the said property at the quoted price, but ultimately failed to deposit the price money to the Bank in spite of repeated call by the Bank. As a result of which the Respondent No.4 Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 2005 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj for recovery of the Bank dues against the borrower and the mortgagors. The said Suit was decreed on contest by Judgment and Decree dated 8-4-2007. 

 4. After passing the decree, the Petitioner filed an application on 23-4-2007 before the Respondent No.4 Bank requesting them to sell the aforesaid 8 decimals land owned by Anil Kumar to him as co-sharer of the plot and possessing the same jointly and to receive the proportionate amount of decretal money from the Petitioner. But the Respondent No.4 Bank did not allow the Petitioner to purchase the property at the quoted price. Subsequently, the Respondent No.5 at the back of the Petitioner filed an application in the trial Court on 26-4-2007 without serving any copy to the Petitioner praying for a direction upon the Decree holder Bank to sell the property to his representative named Khairunnessa at the quoted price found in the auction held under section 12(3) of the Ain before filing of the Suit. The trial Court allowed the same by the Impugned Order dated 26-4-2007 directing the Bank to execute and register the kabala in favour of one Khairunnessa within 10 days of the Order and to deliver possession of the mortgaged property to the said purchaser. At this stage, the Petitioner being aggrieved by the said Order, moved this Court by filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay. 

 5. The Respondent No. 4 Bank and Respondent No. 5 contested the Rule by filing separate Affidavits-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations made in the application. The Respondent No.4 Bank contended that the Court below failed to consider that, after pronouncement of the Judgment and drawing up of the decree, it has become functus officio and yet, it most arbitrarily passed the Impugned Order allowing the application filed by the Respondent No.5. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat committed gross illegality in allowing the application filed by the Defendant Respondent No.5 directing the Decree holder Bank to sell the mortgaged property in question to the representative of Respondent No. 5 within 10 (ten) days. The Respondent Bank did not agree to sell the mortgaged property at the price offered by Defendant Respondent No.5 and the Petitioner, because none of the guarantors have had any right to purchase the mortgaged property at the price quoted in the auction held under section 12(3) of the Ain. Further case of the Respondent No.4 are that the Court has had no jurisdiction to pass any order after pronouncement of the Judgment and Decree unless an execution case is filed by the Decree holder Bank for recovery of the money from the Judgment-Debtors by selling the mortgaged property through auction under section 33 of the Ain and, as such the Impugned Order is palpably illegal and passed without jurisdiction. 

 6. The Respondent No.5 contended that the Petitioner neither owner of the property in question nor any property owned by him was directed to be sold and, as such the Petitioner is not an aggrieved person within the meaning of Article 102 of the Constitution and, as such the writ petition is not maintainable in law, rather it has been filed with an ulterior motive to harass Respondent No. 5 and his representative, The Respondent No. 4 Bank accepted the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 2005 and put the said decree in execution by filing Execution Case No. 32 of 2007 for recovery of the decretal money and, as such by the Impugned Order, the Decree- holder Bank has not in any way prejudiced. It is also stated that the Artha Rin Adalat passed the Impugned Order keeping conformity with the decree passed by it, hence there is no illegality in the Impugned Order and, by' the said order the Petitioner as well as the Decree-holder Bank had nothing to lose. Further case of the Respondent No.5 are that, after holding auction under section 12(3) of the Ain, the Bank offered 8 decimals of land owned by Anil Kumar to the highest bidder at the price quoted by him but the highest bidder did not come forward to accept proposal of the Bank as the property offered to him are joint property, 

 7. Thereafter, the Bank proposed the Petitioner to purchase the property at the price quoted in the auction, but' the Petitioner did not come forward to accept the proposal of the Bank. Subsequently, the Bank proposed to Respondent No.5 to purchase the property in question at the price quoted by the highest bidder. The Respondent No. 5 expressed his willingness to purchase the property, but the Bank at a point of time did not come forward to materialize the proposal made by it and filed the Suit before the Artha Rin Adalat against the borrower, present Petitioner and the Respondent No.5. The said Suit was decreed and the Artha Rin Adalat, in its judgment, specifically observed that the property was offered to the Respondent No.5 by the Bank at the price quoted by the highest bidder and the Respondent No.5 expressed his willingness to purchase the property. In this situation, Respondent No.5 filed an application before the Artha Rin Adalat on 26-4-2007 praying for a direction upon the Bank to execute a kabala and register the same in favour of the representative of the Respondent No.5 namely, Khairunnessa. 

 8. The trial Court allowed the said application and directed Respondent No.4 Bank to execute and register the sale deed in favour of said Khairunnessa. But the Bank failed to comply with the order passed by the Court. Consequently, the Court executed a deed of sale and registered the same in favour of Respondent No. 5's representative and delivered possession of the property to her and, as such the Court below committee no illegality, and did nothing detrimental to the interest of the Petitioner and the Decree holder Bank: Therefore, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. Mr MA Quayyum Chowdhury, the learned advocate appearing for the Petitioner submits that the, trial Court, after pronouncement of the judgment and drawing up the decree has become functus officio and, as such the trial Court cannot pass any order in the said proceeding giving any relief to any party to the suit. However, in the instant case, the Artha Rin Adalat not only reopened the- proceeding afresh, but also gave relief to the, Judgment Debtor who is not the beneficiary, of the decree. He also submits that after passing the decree, the trial Court cannot pass any order except correction of clerical or are thmatical error in the decree passed. It is also argued that unless an execution case is filed by the Decree holder to execute decree, the Court has no jurisdiction and or authority to pass any order in aid of the Decree holder or the Judgment Debtor. But in the instant case, the Artha Rin Adalat most illegally passed the order after pronouncement of the judgment on an application filed by a Judgment Debtor directing the Decree holder Bank to sell the property to a person who was not a party to the proceeding nor a guarantor or participant in the auction held before filing of the suit and, as such the Impugned Order is illegal and passed without jurisdiction. 

 11. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No.4 Bank submits that the order passed by the Court below is apparently illegal and without lawful authority, on the ground that after pronouncement of the judgment and drawing up of the decree by the trial Court, it has had no jurisdiction to pass any order except correction of clerical mistake. The trial Court after passing the decree, allowed an application filed by a Judgment Debtor and directed the Decree holder to execute a sale deed and register the same in favour of a person not connected with the proceeding within 10 days. But according to law, the trial Court, after passing the judgment and signing of the decree, has become functus officio. Therefore, the trial Court cannot pass any order in aid of any party to the proceeding or to their detriment and, as such the orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat after passing the Judgment and Decree are required to be declared illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 12. Mr Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr S Rashed Jahangir, the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 5 submit that the trial Court in passing the Impugned Order has not committed any illegality or error in law. Referring to the relevant portion of the judgment passed by the trial Court, Mr Alam submits that the Court in the judgment clearly observed that the property in question was 'once placed in auction by the Bank under section 12(3) of the Ain before filing of the Suit and the Bank offered the property in question to the Respondent No.5 at the price quoted by the highest bidder. The Respondent No.5, in response to the offer made by the Decree holder Bank, expressed his willingness to purchase the property in writing, but ultimately the Bank did not come forward to sell the property to Respondent NO.5 and filed the Artha Rin Suit against the Respondent No.5 along with others for recovery of the Bank dues. Referring to, the Operative portion of the judgment, Mr Alarri tried to impress upon the Court that the trial Court, while passing the decree, clearly directed the Bank to sell the property in question and to execute the sale deed in favour of the purchaser and deliver possession of the same to him. 

 13. Pursuant to the decree passed by the trial Court, the Respondent No.5 filed an application before the trial Court seeking direction upon the Bank to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the Respondent No. 5's representative. The trial Court, upon considering all the facts and circumstances, allowed the same and directed the Decree holder Bank to execute sale deed in favour of the representative of the Respondent No.5 within the time fixed in the Impugned Order. But the Bank failed to comply with the same and ultimately the representative of the Respondent No.5 got the kabala registered through Court and delivery of possession of the property. Therefore, there was no illegality at all. In fact by the said order and the subsequent act of the Court, it has implemented .its verdict and by the Impugned, Order, the Petitioner as well as the Decree Holder has not in any way been prejudiced and as such the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 15. In the present case the only question which now arises is whether the Court, after pronouncement of judgment and drawing up of the decree, has any jurisdiction to pass further order in the same proceeding allowing or rejecting any application when it has become functus officio. 

 16. The Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 2005 against the Borrower and the guarantors for recovery of loan and the said suit was decreed on 8-4-2007 (decree signed on 15-4-2007) in favour of the Bank and against the defendants. 

 17. On perusal of the Judgment and Decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, it appears that the Court passed the decree following the provisions of section 12(6) of the Ain deducting the price of 8 decimals mortgaged property of the Borrower on the basis of price quoted in the auction held under section 12(3) of the A in before filing of the Suit. It does not mean that after passing the decree, the mortgaged property should be sold to a Judgment Debtor who once i.e. before filing of the suit expressed his willingness to purchase the land at the price quoted in' auction and subsequently failed to purchase the property upon payment of the price money in spite of repeated requests and reminders of the Bank Decree Holder. The law is simple, when the Bank, before filing of the Suit had placed the property on auction and the said process failed, it means that the said process of auction ended there. In the aforesaid circumstances, the Artha Rin Adalat cannot direct the Decree holder Bank to sell the property to the defendant Judgment Debtor who did not come forward to purchase the property at the price quoted in the auction held before filing of the suit. It is in this court's opinion that when the Court deducted the price of land from the claim of the Bank under section 12(6) of the Ain, the title of the land shall vest in the Bank under section 33(7) of the Ain as per provision contained in section 12(7) which runs thus; 

 19. In the instant case, the Artha Rin Adalat after becoming functus officio sat over the decree again as a trial Court and proceeded further at the instance of a Judgment debtor who is not a beneficiary of the decree. Where a final decree f has been passed, the Court has become functusr officio, it cannot alter and amend the decree except correcting clerical and are thrnatical error under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it also cannot proceed further or extend its hand in aid of the Judgment Debtor unless the f Decree is put in execution by the Decree holder. But in the present case, the trial Court, after passing decree, proceeded further in aid of the Judgment Debtor and executed a sale deed in favour of a person who is not party to the 

 20. Admittedly, there was no appeal at the instance of any party against the decree passed by the trial Court. It implies that the Judgment and Decree of the trial Court has become final. The trial Court, after passing the decree and signing it, passed the Impugned Order on 26-4-2007 allowing the application of the Respondent No.5 (Defendant No.4 in Suit) directing the Decree holder-Bank to sell the mortgaged property to the representative of Respondent No.5 and to execute the sale deed in her favour within 10 days from the date of order. In our view, the trial Court, ex facie, had no jurisdiction to pass such order. Once the decree is signed by the Court, it has become functus officio and it has no jurisdiction to do what is prohibited (expressly or impliedly) by the Code so as to defeat the statutory provisions of law. Law does not invest the Court with jurisdiction over the matters which are excluded of its cognizance. Where a specific provisions are contained with regard' to particular procedure under the law, the Court has no power to make such provisions meaningless and to devise its own procedure. 

 21. The general rule is that a final decision of a Court cannot be reopened. The expression functus officio means having discharged a duty. It may also mean whose duty or authority has come to an end. The trial Court has ceased to have any jurisdiction in respect of the matter once the Judgment and Decree in the Suit had been rendered. 

 22. There can be no controversy that when a decree has been passed by a Court, it has no further jurisdiction to adjudicate upon it or to pass any further order. In the present case, the trial Court exceeded its jurisdiction and most illegally reopened the proceeding afresh by entertaining an application filed by the Judgment Debtor and allowing the same by the Impugned Order. 

 23. It is to be noted that the Petitioner, by an application dated 7-5-2007, prayed for recalling the Impugned Order No. 50 and prayed for selling the property to the Petitioner on the ground that he is a co-sharer of the property in question and the property is undemarceted. The Court below, by its Order No. 54 dated 14-5-2007, rejected the prayer of the Petitioner and directed the Respondent No. 5 to deposit the price money to the Bank. Thereafter, the Petitioner moved this Court against the Order passed by the trial Court and obtained the present Rule and Order of stay on 29- 5-2007. The trial Court fixed 25-6-2007 for submitting stay order of this Court. Subsequently, the trial Court on an application of the Bank, made the decree final by its Order No. 60 dated 8- 10-2007 though there is no provisions in the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 2003 requiring the Court to make the decree final, where the suit was not a Mortgage Suit for foreclosure under section 5(3) of the Ain. 

 25. It is also noted that the Suit was not filed by the defendant seeking a decree for specific performance of contract and no decree to that effect had ever been passed by the Court. Therefore, we are astonished and fail to understand how and under what provisions of law the Artha Rin Adalat could direct the Decree holder to execute a sale deed in favour of the person who is not a party to the proceeding and how it could execute a sale deed in favour of a stranger during subsistence of stay order of this Court.
